proposals.before: At King Cheng’s command, the Duke of Zhou Dan raised troops against Yin, killed Wu Geng Lu Fu and Guan Shu, banished Cai Shu, and enfeoffed Kang Shu with Wu Geng’s remaining Yin people.
proposals.after: At King Cheng’s command, the Duke of Zhou Dan raised troops against Yin, killed Wu Geng Lu Fu and Guan Shu, banished Cai Shu, and with Wu Geng’s remaining Yin people enfeoffed Kang Shu as lord of Wei, to dwell in the former Shang ruins between the He and Qi rivers.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits 為衛君 and 居河、淇閒故商墟, which state the Wei lordship and the residence in the former Shang ruins between the rivers.

proposals.before: Duke Qing ascended for twelve years and died. His son Duke Xi ascended.
proposals.after: Duke Qing reigned for twelve years and died. His son Duke Xi ascended.
proposals.reason: 立十二年卒 means he was on the throne twelve years, not that he 'ascended for twelve years.'

proposals.before: Gong Bo younger brother He had favor with Xi Hou, much gave him bribes;
proposals.after: Gong Bo's younger brother He had favor with Marquis Xi, who gave him many gifts;
proposals.reason: The literal English is ungrammatical and reverses the gift-giver; 多予之賂 is Duke Xi giving gifts to He.

proposals.before: In the fifth year of Duke Zhuang's reign, he married a Qi woman as his wife. He loved her but she had no son.
proposals.after: In the fifth year of Duke Zhuang's reign, he married a Qi woman as his wife. She was beautiful but had no son.
proposals.reason: Chinese 好而無子 describes the wife as beautiful and childless, not the duke's affection.

proposals.before: In Duke Zhuang's fifth year, he took a Qi woman as his wife. He loved her but she had no son.
proposals.after: In Duke Zhuang's fifth year, he took a Qi woman as his wife. She was beautiful but had no son.
proposals.reason: Literal 好 is 'beautiful' modifying the Qi woman, parallel to the idiomatic error.

proposals.before: When he heard their slander, he was furious. He then sent Crown Prince Ji to Qi and ordered robbers to block him at the border and kill him. He gave the crown prince a white banner as a token.
proposals.after: When he heard their slander, he was furious. He then sent Crown Prince Ji to Qi and ordered robbers to block him at the border and kill him. He gave the crown prince a white banner, and told the border robbers to kill whoever held the white banner.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 而告界盜見持白旄者殺之, the token instruction that the following narrative requires.

proposals.before: Lord Qian Mou of Wei reigned for eight years. Duke Xiang of Qi, acting on the king’s command, led the feudal lords in a joint attack on Wei, restored Duke Hui of Wei, and executed the left and right ministers.
proposals.after: Lord Qian Mou of Wei reigned for eight years. Duke Xiang of Qi, acting on the king’s command, led the feudal lords in a joint attack on Wei, restored Duke Hui of Wei, and executed the left and right princes.
proposals.reason: 左右公子 are the left and right princes, not ministers; the literal field already has princes.

proposals.before: King Hui of Zhou fled to Wen. Wei and Yan established King Hui's younger brother Kui as wang.
proposals.after: King Hui of Zhou fled to Wen. Wei and Yan established King Hui's younger brother Kui as king.
proposals.reason: Leaving wang untranslated obscures that Kui was installed as king.

proposals.before: Initially, when the Di killed Duke Yi, the people of Wei pitied him and thought of again installing a descendant of Duke Xuan’s deceased former crown prince Ji. Ji’s son had also died, so they installed his younger brother Shen, making him Duke Dai.
proposals.after: Initially, when the Di killed Duke Yi, the people of Wei pitied him and thought of again installing a descendant of Duke Xuan’s deceased former crown prince Ji. Ji’s son had also died, and Shou, who had died in Ji’s place, also had no son.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English invents the installation of Shen as Duke Dai, which belongs to neighboring sentences, and omits 子壽又無子.

proposals.before: Crown Prince Ji had two half-brothers from the same mother: one was called Qian Mou. Qian Mou once replaced Duke Hui as lord, and after eight years again left;
proposals.after: Crown Prince Ji had two younger brothers from the same mother: one was called Qian Mou. Qian Mou once replaced Duke Hui as lord, and after eight years again left;
proposals.reason: 同母弟 means younger brothers by the same mother; half-brothers is an unwarranted narrowing.

proposals.before: The grand officer Yuan Tiao attacked Duke Cheng, and Duke Cheng fled.
proposals.after: The grand officer Yuan Xuan attacked Duke Cheng, and Duke Cheng fled.
proposals.reason: 元咺 is Yuan Xuan (咺 = xuān), not Tiao; the English personal name is a phonetic error.

proposals.before: Grand officer Yuan Tiao attacked Duke Cheng, and Duke Cheng fled.
proposals.after: Grand officer Yuan Xuan attacked Duke Cheng, and Duke Cheng fled.
proposals.reason: 元咺 is Yuan Xuan (咺 = xuān), not Tiao; the English personal name is a phonetic error.

proposals.before: Then Zhou pleaded on his behalf with Duke Wen of Jin. He finally re-entered Wei, executed Yuan Tiao, and Wei lord Xia fled.
proposals.after: Then Zhou pleaded on his behalf with Duke Wen of Jin. He finally re-entered Wei, executed Yuan Xuan, and Wei lord Xia fled.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 元咺 as Yuan Tiao instead of Yuan Xuan.

proposals.before: Then Zhou requested on his behalf to Duke Wen of Jin. He finally entered Wei, and executed Yuan Tiao. Wei lord Xia fled.
proposals.after: Then Zhou requested on his behalf to Duke Wen of Jin. He finally entered Wei, and executed Yuan Xuan. Wei lord Xia fled.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 元咺 as Yuan Tiao instead of Yuan Xuan.

proposals.before: In the twenty-sixth year, Bing Chan of Qi assassinated their lord Duke Yi.
proposals.after: In the twenty-sixth year, Bing Chu of Qi assassinated their lord Duke Yi.
proposals.reason: 邴歜 is Bing Chu (歜 = chù); Chan does not match the Chinese given name.

proposals.before: In the twenty-sixth year, Qi's Bing Chan assassinated their lord Duke Yi.
proposals.after: In the twenty-sixth year, Qi's Bing Chu assassinated their lord Duke Yi.
proposals.reason: 邴歜 is Bing Chu (歜 = chù); Chan does not match the Chinese given name.

proposals.before: The concubine, with favor, hated Cao to the duke. The duke also whipped Cao three hundred times.
proposals.after: The concubine used her favor to speak ill of Cao to the duke. The duke also whipped Cao three hundred times.
proposals.reason: 惡曹於公 is slander before the duke, not 'hated Cao to the duke'.

proposals.before: The day grew late without summons, and they went to shoot geese in the park.
proposals.after: The day grew late without summons, and he went to shoot geese in the park.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 而去射鴻於囿 is Duke Xian, not the two ministers.

proposals.before: The two sons followed him. The duke did not remove his hunting clothes and spoke with them.
proposals.after: The two men followed him. The duke did not remove his hunting clothes and spoke with them.
proposals.reason: 二子 here is the two ministers, not biological sons.

proposals.before: The two sons were angered and went to Su.
proposals.after: The two men were angered and went to Su.
proposals.reason: 二子 continues to mean Sun Wenzi and Ning Huizi, not sons.

proposals.before: Sun Wen Zi's son often served the duke drinks and made Shi Cao sing the final stanza of clever words."
proposals.after: Sun Wenzi's son often served the duke drinks and made Shi Cao sing the final stanza of 'Clever Words'.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quote; 巧言 is the song title, not generic 'clever words'.

proposals.before: Duke Shangqiu took the throne and enfeoffed Sun Wenzi Linfu at Su.
proposals.after: Duke Shang, Qiu, took the throne and enfeoffed Sun Wenzi Linfu at Su.
proposals.reason: 殤公秋 is Duke Shang, personal name Qiu, not a fused 'Shangqiu'.

proposals.before: When he passed Su, Sun Lin Fu struck the stone chimes for him and said, "This is not joyous music; the tone is deeply mournful. This is what will bring disorder to Wei."
proposals.after: When he passed Su, Sun Linfu struck the stone chimes for him. He said, "This is not joyous music; the tone is deeply mournful. This is what will bring disorder to Wei."
proposals.reason: The judgment on the music is the visiting envoy's; the English fuses it onto Sun Linfu after 為擊磬.

proposals.before: In the twelfth year, initially Kong Yuwen Zi married the crown prince Kuai Kui's sister, and she gave birth to Pei.
proposals.after: In the twelfth year—this had happened earlier—Kong Yu, posthumously Kong Wenzi, married the crown prince Kuai Kui's sister, and she gave birth to Kui.
proposals.reason: 悝 is Kong Kui, not Pei; 初 marks a flashback to the marriage and birth.

proposals.before: In the twelfth year, initially Kong Yuwen Zi took the crown prince Kuai Kui's sister and gave birth to Pei.
proposals.after: In the twelfth year, originally Kong Yu Wenzi took the crown prince Kuai Kui's sister to wife, and she gave birth to Kui.
proposals.reason: The sister, not Kong Yu, gave birth; 悝 is Kui.

proposals.before: Hun Liangfu, an attendant of the Kong clan, was handsome and capable. After Kong Wenzi died, Liangfu had relations with Pei’s mother.
proposals.after: Hun Liangfu, an attendant of the Kong clan, was handsome. After Kong Wenzi died, Liangfu had illicit relations with Kui's mother.
proposals.reason: 悝 is Kui; 通 is illicit intercourse.

proposals.before: The Kong clan's elder Luan Ning asked him, and he called the marriage concubine to tell him.
proposals.after: The Kong clan's elder Luan Ning asked them, and they identified themselves as in-law concubines in reply.
proposals.reason: 称姻妾以告 means they claimed to be marital concubines.

proposals.before: After the meal, Pei’s mother took a ge spear and went first. The crown prince followed with five armored men, carrying Xi with him.
proposals.after: After the meal, Kui's mother took a ge-halberd and went first. The crown prince and five armored men followed, with a sacrificial boar borne along.
proposals.reason: 輿猳 is a boar for the covenant, not a person named Xi.

proposals.before: He summoned guards and harnessed the chariot. They passed around wine and roast, and escorted Duke Chu Zhe as he fled to Lu.
proposals.after: Shao Hu harnessed the chariot. They passed around wine and roast, and escorted Duke Chu Zhe as he fled to Lu.
proposals.reason: 召護 is a personal name, not a command to summon guards.

proposals.before: He summoned protection and harnessed the chariot. They circulated wine and drank roast, served Duke Chu Zhe who fled to Lu.
proposals.after: Shao Hu drove the chariot. They circulated the wine-cup and ate the roast, and served Duke Chu Zhe, who fled to Lu.
proposals.reason: 召護 names the driver; 食炙 is eating the roast.

proposals.before: Zi Lu said, "Why does the crown prince employ Kong Pei?
proposals.after: Zi Lu said, "Why does the crown prince use Kong Kui?
proposals.reason: 孔悝 is Kong Kui, not Kong Pei.

proposals.before: Kong Pei finally installed Crown Prince Kuaikui, who became Duke Zhuang.
proposals.after: Kong Kui finally installed Crown Prince Kuai Kui, who became Duke Zhuang.
proposals.reason: 孔悝 is Kong Kui.

proposals.before: Di's father was Duke Jing.
proposals.after: Shi's father was Duke Jing.
proposals.reason: The same man is Prince Shi (公子適) in the previous sentence; rendering 適 as Di here breaks the identity with the established English name.

proposals.before: Wei changed course and installed the heir lord’s younger brother, who became Lord Yuan.
proposals.after: Wei then installed Lord Si’s younger brother, who became Lord Yuan.
proposals.reason: 嗣君 is the specific ruler Lord Si, not a generic heir-lord, and 更立 means installing a replacement rather than changing course.

proposals.before: Grand Historian said: I read hereditary houses speak, arrived at Xuan Gong crown prince because wife seen executed, younger brother Shou contended death to yield each other, this with Jin crown prince Shen Sheng dared not clarify Li Ji transgression same, both disliked injure father intention.
proposals.after: The Grand Historian said: I read the hereditary-house accounts, and when I reached Duke Xuan's crown prince who was executed because of his wife, and the younger brother Shou who contended over dying in mutual yielding, this was the same as Jin's crown prince Shen Sheng not daring to make clear Li Ji's fault; both disliked injuring their father's will.
proposals.reason: The current literal English is ungrammatical and obscures the comparison and the two Wei princes.

proposals.before: Yet finally died death, how sad!
proposals.after: Yet in the end they died. How sad it is!
proposals.reason: The doubled died/death calque is ungrammatical and hides that the silent subject is the princes just named.

decisions.reason: The idiomatic English omits 為衛君 and 居河、淇閒故商墟. The replacement restores Kang Shu’s Wei lordship and residence in the former Shang ruins between the He and Qi without adding unsupported matter.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以武庚殷餘民封康叔為衛君，居河、淇閒故商墟

decisions.reason: 立十二年卒 marks twelve years on the throne, not an act of ascending that lasted twelve years. “Reigned for twelve years and died” is the accurate literal rendering.
The original is ungrammatical and leaves the giver of 賂 unclear. 有寵於釐侯，多予之賂 is He favored by Marquis Xi, who gave him many gifts; the replacement restores agent and sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 共伯弟和有寵於釐侯，多予之賂

decisions.reason: 好而無子 is predicated of the Qi wife (beautiful and childless), matching the following 生子 of the Chen wife. “He loved her” invents the duke’s affection.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 取齊女為夫人，好而無子

decisions.reason: In this sentence 好 describes the Qi woman as beautiful, not the duke’s loving her. The literal field needs the same correction as the idiomatic.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 取齊女為夫人，好而無子

decisions.reason: The original collapses 與太子白旄，而告界盜見持白旄者殺之 into a vague “token” and drops the robbers’ recognition order, which the next sentence presupposes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與太子白旄，而告界盜見持白旄者殺之

decisions.reason: 左右公子 are the left and right princes, already so rendered in the preceding unit. “Ministers” is a rank error.

為王 is already represented in the literal by “as wang,” the same calque used for 侯 as hou in neighboring units. The idiomatic field already says “king”; leaving wang in the literal is a register choice, not a semantic error.
This unit ends at 子壽又無子. The original invents Shen’s installation as Duke Dai (from later sentences) and omits that Shou, who died in Ji’s place, also had no son.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 伋子又死，而代伋死者子壽又無子

decisions.reason: 同母弟 are younger brothers by the same mother. “Half-brothers” wrongly implies they did not share a father; these sons of Duke Xuan are uterine younger brothers, not half-brothers.
元咺 is Yuan Xuan (咺, xuān). Tiao is a false reading of the given name.
The same name 元咺 must be Yuan Xuan in the literal field as well.
誅元咺 is the execution of Yuan Xuan, not Yuan Tiao.
The literal likewise misreads 元咺 as Tiao; Xuan is the correct English form.
邴歜 is Bing Chu (歜, chù). Chan does not match the character.
The literal field repeats the same false reading of 歜 as Chan.
惡曹於公 is to speak ill of Cao before the duke, not “hated Cao to the duke.” The replacement restores the slander construction.
The silent subject of 而去射鴻於囿 is Duke Xian; 二子從之 in the next unit shows the ministers followed him. “They went” misassigns the hunt.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 日旰不召，而去射鴻於囿

decisions.reason: 二子 here resumes Sun Wenzi and Ning Huizi, not biological sons of the duke.
二子 continues the same two ministers. Rendering them as “sons” is a kinship error.
The stray closing quote is a corruption, and 巧言 is the poem title, not generic clever words.
殤公秋 is Duke Shang, personal name Qiu, not a fused toponym-like Shangqiu. The preceding unit already separates the posthumous title and the given name.

After the new subject 孫林父為擊磬, 曰 most naturally continues with Sun Linfu as speaker. The proposed “He said” does not actually reassign the speech, and this chapter’s wording does not mark a change of speaker to the visiting envoy.
悝 is Kui, not Pei, and 孔圉文子 is Kong Yu, posthumously Wenzi, not a fused Yuwen. 初 marks the marriage and birth as prior to the twelfth-year narrative.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十二年，初，孔圉文子取太子蒯聵之姊，生悝

decisions.reason: 生悝 is the sister’s giving birth, not Kong Yu’s. The original also misreads 悝 as Pei.
美好 describes appearance, not “capable,” 通於 is illicit intercourse, and 悝 is Kui. The replacement corrects all three without adding matter.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孔氏之豎渾良夫美好，孔文子卒，良夫通於悝母

decisions.reason: 稱姻妾以告 means the disguised pair identified themselves as marital concubines, not that someone summoned a concubine. 問之 refers to the two who had just arrived.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 孔氏之老欒甯問之，稱姻妾以告

decisions.reason: 輿猳 is a boar borne along for the covenant, not a person named Xi. 悝母 is Kui’s mother.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太子與五人介，輿猳從之

decisions.reason: 召護 is the personal name Shao Hu, the driver, not a command to summon guards.
召護 names the charioteer; 食炙 is eating the roast, not drinking it. The original misreads both the name and the verb.

decisions.after: Zi Lu said, "Why does the crown prince employ Kong Kui?
decisions.reason: 孔悝 is Kong Kui, not Kong Pei, but 焉用 is “employ/what use in using,” and the original’s “employ” is accurate. Only the personal name needs repair; keep the rest of the human wording, including the unclosed quotation that continues in the next unit.
孔悝 is Kong Kui. Splitting 蒯聵 as Kuai Kui matches the established English name in this chapter.
適 is the same man named Prince Shi (公子適) in the previous sentence. Rendering him as Di here splits one person into two English names.
嗣君 is the ruler Lord Si, not a generic heir-lord, and 更立 is installing a replacement, not “changing course.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏更立嗣君弟，是為元君

decisions.reason: The current literal is not English. The replacement restores the comparison of Duke Xuan’s crown prince and Shou with Jin’s Shen Sheng, and the shared refusal to injure their fathers’ will.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 至於宣公之太子以婦見誅，弟壽爭死以相讓，此與晉太子申生不敢明驪姬之過同，俱惡傷父之志

decisions.reason: 卒死亡 is that they died in the end, not a doubled “died death.” The silent subject is the princes just named.

claimRetractions.reason: The alternate English name Di was created only by rendering 適 as Di in this unit, contradicting Prince Shi in the previous sentence. No separate source name Di is supported.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Yuan Tiao was produced by misreading 咺; the Chinese and pinyin already identify Yuan Xuan.
The English personal name Bing Chan was produced by misreading 歜; the Chinese and pinyin already identify Bing Chu.
孔圉文子 is Kong Yu with the posthumous Wenzi, not a fused given name Yuwen.
悝 is Kui; Pei is a false English given name created by the bad translation.
悝母 is Kui’s mother; Pei is the same false reading of 悝.
美好 assesses appearance; “capable” was added by the translation and is not in the Chinese.
孔悝 is Kong Kui; Kong Pei is the same false English name as Pei for 悝.
